title: Evaluating an Automated Mediator for Joint Narratives in a Conflict Situation
benchmark_measurement: Measuring attitude changes (willingness to compromise, anger, etc.) between conflicting groups (Israeli Jews and Israeli Arabs) whose conflict involves significant ethnic and religious dimensions.
findings: The study found that using an automated mediator for collaborative storytelling between Israeli Arabs and Israeli Jews led to positive outcomes comparable to a human mediator. Specifically, the intervention resulted in a more positive attitude toward the conflict, a reduction of anger toward the other group (especially for Hebrew speakers), and an increased willingness to learn more about the other side (especially for Arab speakers). The findings concern attitude shifts between groups in a conflict with a religious dimension, rather than specific religious beliefs or biases.
references: Allport, G. W. (1979). The nature of prejudice. Reading, Mass: Addison-Wesley Pub. Co.
